meta_herb: Efficacy and Safety of Astragalus-Containing Traditional Chinese Medicine Combined with Platinum-Based Chemotherapy for Advanced Gastric Cancer: A Systemic review and Meta-Analysis

Gastric cancer (GC) is the fifth-most commonly diagnosed cancer and the third leading cause of cancer-related death in the world. 70% or 80% of the patients with GC are diagnosed at advanced stage and lost the opportunity for surgical treatment. Platinum-based chemotherapy is widely used in the treatment of advanced GC. However, the side effects and the development of resistance to chemotherapy in clinical practice reveal its limitations and have prompted more attention to be paid to the study of complementary treatments.  Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) is the most common complementary therapy for cancer treatment and it has been shown to enhance the efficacy and reduce the side effects of anticancer strategies. Particularly, the Astragalus-based Chinese medicine are frequently combined with chemotherapy for advanced GC in clinic.

Efficacy of Astragalus membranaceus membranaceus (Huang Qi) for cancer-related fatigue:A meta-analysis

According to the American Cancer Society 2020, the number of cancer survivors is steadily increasing.During the active treatment of these cancer survivors, 60-100% of patients experience cancer-related fatigue (CRF) , which has been identified as the most common and distressing complication compared to other symptoms and continues throughout the cancer patient's life cycle.Due to the complexity of the pathogenesis of the disease, there is no clear drug treatment option. The US National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Clinical Guidelines for the treatment of cancer-related fatigue recommends non-pharmacological treatments, such as exercise interventions, sleep therapy, and nutritional supplementation support, as the first choice recommendations for the intervention of patients with cancer-related fatigue.In recent years, the NCCN as well as the Society of Integrative Oncology (SIO) have also recommended that patients with CRF manage symptoms associated with the disease and treatment by adding nutritional supplements, and suggested that some herbal supplements, such as ginseng and Astragalus membranaceus may be helpful in CRF.Astragalus membranaceus polysaccharide (PG2) injection is now also approved as a type of drug therapy for the treatment of cancer-related fatigue in Taiwan patients with advanced cancer.

Cancer survivors experience cancer-causing fatigue in 60-100% of patients undergoing aggressive cancer treatment. At the same time, insomnia, pain and depression have also been shown to be significantly correlated with CRF, severely affecting patients' treatment adherence, recovery process and their quality of life.Nutritional support, one of the techniques commonly used in non-pharmacological interventions, is increasingly being used for symptom management in cancer patients and has been shown to be effective for cancer-caused fatigue and its associated symptoms.To date, no studies have comprehensively and systematically reviewed the effects of treatment with astragalus membranaceus and its extracts alone on fatigue in cancer patients.
